answers.answer: Select 3 randomly chosen Escape Pods for 4 players. Put the lowest-numbered in Section A, the next in B, then alternate A/B; all start Locked side up. The bag starts with 1 Blank, 4 Larvae, 1 Creeper, 1 Queen, 3 Adults, plus 1 additional Adult per player (7 Adults total at four players).
answers.evidence: Setup, board steps 7 and 10.

answers.answer: At setup, remove Corporate and Personal Objective cards marked for more players than are playing, shuffle the decks separately, and deal each player one of each face down. At the First Encounter—the first time an Intruder miniature appears—each player chooses one of their two Objectives and removes the other face down from the game, unseen by anyone. Eggs do not trigger this choice because they are not Intruders.
answers.evidence: Setup step 16; Critical gameplay moments — First Encounter.

answers.answer: Discard the used Action card and two additional Action cards to pay its cost of 2; retain both Contamination cards. Contamination cards can never pay Action costs. For an OR card, choose one section/effect.
answers.evidence: Actions — Action Cost and Actions from Action cards.

answers.answer: They take 1 Light Wound at the end of their own round. Since they pass after taking only one Action, they cannot act again that Player Phase; when passing, they may discard any number of hand cards. They do not take another Fire wound in later players' rounds that turn.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure — Player rounds: Fire applies after finishing own round; passing players take it once and no more that turn.

answers.answer: Flip the unexplored tile face up and reveal its Exploration token; set the Room's Item count to the token's number, oriented toward the board's Item Counter (except Nest and Room Covered In Slime), then resolve its effect and remove the token. Apply the effect before the ordinary Noise roll: Silence suppresses that roll; Danger suppresses it and moves all eligible neighboring Intruders in, or places Noise in each connected corridor if none qualify; other listed effects include Slime, Fire, Malfunction, and Doors. If the destination already contains any Character or Intruder, do not roll Noise. Otherwise a normal roll places a marker in the numbered connected Corridor on 1–4, or resolves Danger/Silence.
answers.evidence: Movement, Rooms, and Corridors; Exploration tokens; Noise roll.

answers.answer: Careful Movement costs 2 Action cards and replaces the post-move Noise roll by placing a Noise marker in a chosen Corridor connected to the destination. It is forbidden in Combat and if every Corridor connected to the destination already has Noise. It follows normal movement restrictions, so a Closed Door blocks passage. Characters cannot stop in Corridors.
answers.evidence: Basic Actions — Careful Movement; Movement, Rooms, and Corridors.

answers.answer: If the roll calls for a Corridor that already has Noise, resolve an Encounter. First discard all Noise markers from Corridors connected to the Room, including the Technical Corridors space if there is an Entrance; draw a token and place the matching Intruder miniature. Set a non-Blank token aside outside the bag (it may return if that Intruder later enters Technical Corridors). Compare its number with the triggering player's hand; fewer cards than the number causes a Surprise Attack. Action and Contamination cards both count for that comparison. A Blank instead places Noise in each connected Corridor and returns to the bag; if it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult if available. Technical Corridors Entrance means the space is treated as a connected Corridor for Noise placement/removal.
answers.evidence: Encounters; Noise roll; Technical Corridors.

answers.answer: Danger moves all neighboring Intruders that are not in Combat with any Character into the Room. If none are eligible, place a Noise marker in every connected Corridor that lacks one (including Technical Corridors if the Room has an Entrance). An Intruder moving into a Character's Room is not an Encounter. Slime changes a Silence result into Danger.
answers.evidence: Exploration tokens — Danger; Noise roll; Encounters; Slime marker.

answers.answer: For a Blank drawn during an Encounter, place a Noise marker in each Corridor connected to that Room, return the Blank to the bag, and end the Encounter without an Intruder appearing. If it was the last token in the bag, add an Adult token if available. During bag development, a Blank adds an Adult token if available and then returns to the bag; it does not place Corridor Noise.
answers.evidence: Encounters — Blank token in an Encounter; Intruder bag development.

answers.answer: Both Intruders stay in their original Room and destroy the Closed Door simultaneously. A destroyed Door lies down, permits movement, and cannot be closed again (except with Plasma Torch). A Noise-triggered appearance through a Closed Door is not blocked; the Intruder appears regardless.
answers.evidence: Fire, Malfunction, Doors, Slime and Noise markers — Door tokens.

answers.answer: When an Intruder moves to a Technical Corridors Entrance, remove its miniature, discard all its Injury markers, and return its token to the bag; any Noise marker in the Technical Corridors space stays. Characters cannot use Technical Corridors except via the named Mechanic Action card or Technical Corridor Plans Item, and Doors cannot be placed there.
answers.evidence: Technical Corridors.

answers.answer: Shoot costs 1 Action card and 1 Ammo; target one Intruder in your Room. It does not add a Contamination card. A miss has no effect. A two-hit die result deals 2 Injuries when Shooting, before Weapon modifications. Melee costs 1 Action card and adds one Contamination card; any miss also causes the Character a Serious Wound, and the two-hit result is treated as 1 Injury.
answers.evidence: Combat — Shoot and Melee Attack.

answers.answer: After damage, 1 Injury kills a Larva or Egg. For Creeper/Adult draw one Intruder Attack card and compare its blood value to current Injury markers; for Breeder/Queen draw two and add their blood values. If the blood value is equal to or lower than injuries, the Intruder dies. Place a Carcass for every dead Intruder except Larvae. If a death-check card shows a Retreat arrow, draw an Event card and move the Intruder along the Corridor number in its movement section; Queen/Breeders retreat if either card has the arrow.
answers.evidence: Combat — Intruder Injuries and death; Intruder Retreat.

answers.answer: Before moving, resolve one Intruder Attack per Intruder in the Room, targeting the escaper. If the Character dies, their Corpse remains in the Room they tried to leave. If they survive, complete the move to the neighboring Room; if it is empty, roll Noise, and if unexplored, explore it normally.
answers.evidence: Combat — Character Escape.

answers.answer: The target is the Character with the fewest Action cards in hand; ties go to the First Player token holder or next player in turn order. Draw an Intruder Attack card: if its symbol matches the attacking Intruder, resolve its effect, otherwise it misses. A Larva does not draw an Attack card: remove its miniature, put it on the target's Character board, and give the target one Contamination card, placed on top of their Action discard pile.
answers.evidence: Combat — Intruder Attack and Infest (Larva attack); Contamination cards and Infection.

answers.answer: At 3 Serious Wounds, dressing one does not prevent death from any further Wound because dressed cards still count toward the three-wound limit. Without dressing, a third Light Wound clears the Light Wound track and causes a Serious Wound. Heal removes a Light Wound or a Dressed Serious Wound as specified by the healing effect. On death, put a Character Corpse token in the Room and drop all Heavy Objects there.
answers.evidence: Character Wounds and death.

answers.answer: Canteen and Shower scan only Contamination cards in the hand and remove all non-Infected cards; an Infected result places a Larva on the board, or kills the Character and places a Creeper in the Room if a Larva is already there. Surgery scans all Contamination cards in the deck, hand, and discard pile, removes all Infected cards, and removes a Larva if present. Then the Character suffers 1 Light Wound, automatically passes, and shuffles all cards (including their full hand and remaining Contamination cards) into their Action deck; their hand stays empty until next turn.
answers.evidence: Room Actions — Surgery, Canteen, Shower Room; Contamination cards and Infection.

answers.answer: Against uncarried Eggs, Shoot or Melee resolves as an attack and each Injury destroys one Egg. Melee against Eggs never draws Contamination and a miss causes no Wound. A Grenade destroys 2 Eggs and a Molotov Cocktail destroys 1. After every attempt to destroy an Egg, roll Noise. Fire in the Room destroys 1 uncarried Egg during each Fire Damage step. When no Eggs remain, the Nest is destroyed.
answers.evidence: Eggs and the Nest.

answers.answer: Use the Evacuation Section A/B Room Action, costing 2 Action cards, to try to board an Unlocked Pod with an available Character space. Make a Noise roll first; if an Intruder appears or is already in the Evacuation Section Room, or if that Room has a Malfunction, entry is not allowed. Each Pod holds up to 2 Characters; Heavy Objects take no Character space. After entry, launch immediately or wait. While waiting, launch at the start of your first round in each Player Phase or exit for free; if you do not launch in your round, you automatically pass. If an Intruder appears in the Evacuation Section Room while you wait, all Pod occupants return to that Room. Another Character entering the Pod may launch it immediately.
answers.evidence: Escape Pods; Room Actions — Evacuation Section A/B.

answers.answer: Victory checks are Engines, Coordinates, Contamination, then Objectives. If 2 or 3 Engines are Damaged, the ship explodes and hibernating Characters die. If the ship is not headed to Earth, hibernating Characters die, except a Character with the Quarantine Objective survives if the destination is Mars. Each surviving Character, whether hibernating or evacuated, undergoes the Contamination check. If they have a Larva, skip scanning step A and resolve the draw step B directly. Thus pod passengers do need Contamination checks.
answers.evidence: Victory Check.
